title: The Vietnam War Redux
author: Tom Engelhardt
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/annie-
spratt-8INM5aoxKWs-unsplash-680x469.jpg)

Image by Annie Spratt.

Honestly, you couldn’t make this world up, could you? Before 2016, in what
grim fantasy (or comedy) would Donald Trump ever have appeared as president of
the United States? Once upon a time, I couldn’t have imagined such a
possibility (and neither, I’m sure, could you!). Once upon a time, it would
have been too absurd even to work as a joke.

And if you had told me, at age 24, when I [turned in my draft
card](https://tomdispatch.com/engelhardt-i-f-stone-and-the-urge-to-serve/) to
protest the then-ongoing war in Vietnam, that, almost 60 years later, my
country, led by -- yes, indeed! -- President Donald J. Trump, would be
fighting yet another ludicrous war, thousands of miles away, that no one, not
even the president of the United States, could explain, I would have thought
you balmy. Honestly, I can’t believe that my country is now making war on and
threatening further war against -- of all places on Earth -- Iran. On this
planet at this moment, it just makes no sense. Or perhaps what I really mean
is: no more sense than having Donald Trump as president of the United States
for a second time.

Back in the 1960s and early 1970s, we were already experiencing a totally mad
and brutal set of conflicts, including, of course -- or do I mean, of coarse?
-- those underway against Vietnam’s neighbors, Cambodia and Laos, in which --
can you even believe it today? -- [hundreds of
thousands](https://theconversation.com/henry-kissingers-bombing-campaign-
likely-killed-hundreds-of-thousands-of-cambodians-and-set-path-for-the-
ravages-of-the-khmer-rouge-209353) of people would die. And all of those
countries were indeed thousands of miles (and lame-brained justifications)
away from the United States. Just try to imagine that this country’s military
dropped [at least two million tons](https://www.history.com/articles/laos-
most-bombed-country-vietnam-war) of cluster bombs on Laos alone in those
years, more than all the bombs dropped during World War II combined.

And now, having evidently learned no lessons whatsoever from such disastrous
wars, somehow the United States -- and yes, it’s too weird not to be put in
italics! --  _under the_  _leadership_ of  _Donald J. Trump_ is at it again.

Of course, even well before that Vietnam moment, my country had already become
a distinctly “great” global imperial power -- there had never truly been one
quite like it -- that was garrisoning its military (as it still is) on
literally [hundreds and hundreds of bases](https://tomdispatch.com/the-all-
american-base-world/) in scores of countries globally and would end up using
that military all too often in the post-World War II era. After all, when I
was just six years old, the U.S. started fighting a war thousands of miles
away in -- yes, [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War)! That, of
course, was in 1950, and like the conflicts that would follow into our own era
-- and here I’m thinking, for instance, of Donald Trump’s ongoing, if little
written about, [bombing campaign against
Somalia](https://news.antiwar.com/2026/08/03/us-launches-airstrike-in-somalia-
for-77th-time-this-year/) (yes, Somalia!) -- success was never in the cards.
So, in some eerie sense, there’s really nothing new (and something all too
predictable) about a war with Iran today, don’t you think?

Oh, except, of course, that this country now has a unique version of a madman
for its president and his present war, like all wars, has been pouring fossil
fuels (whose climate-warming harm he’s
[labelled](https://time.com/7319744/trump-un-speech-climate-change/) a “scam”
and “the greatest con job ever perpetuated”) into the atmosphere of a planet
that, unlike in my youth, has started to broil in a big-time fashion. (If you
don’t believe me, [ask
Europeans](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/31/wildfires-extreme-
weather-europe-spain-france-climate-crisis-analysis) nearing the end of a
wildly overheated summer there.) And that, in turn, ensures that Donald Trump
can make war not just (like so many presidents before him) on specific
countries like Iran, but on all of us and on Planet Earth itself.

And of course, to ensure that this piece doesn’t become too ludicrously long,
as I explore the history of American military bases and wars to the present
moment, I’m going to have to leave out all too many all-American conflicts in
the decades since Vietnam (Laos and Cambodia) ended, including in Afghanistan,
Iraq, Libya, Somalia (where US Africa Command had just [launched its 78th
airstrike](https://news.antiwar.com/2026/08/09/us-bombs-somalia-for-78th-time-
this-year/) of the year as I was writing this)**,** and**** Yemen, [among
other
places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_wars_involving_the_United_States_in_the_21st_century).
(And that’s not even to mention such passing moments as the relatively recent
Trumpian bombings in -- yes! --
[Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_intervention_in_Nigeria).)

The world, it seems, is now the president’s target-practice range and his set
of killings globally, as Nick Turse recently [pointed
out](https://theintercept.com/2026/08/05/trump-colonial-extermination-
asymmetric-warfare/), with their asymmetrical body counts in which almost no
Americans die but stunning numbers of the Other go down, distinctly harken
back to the slaughters of people of color in the colonial age. As he put it,
“our” president has “made disproportionate slaughter his signature
accomplishment from Latin America to the Middle East to Africa.” And this,
mind you, is the guy who [bragged](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2026/jun/08/what-trump-actually-said-no-war-promise) in 2023 between his
two terms in office that “I was the only president in modern history who did
not have any new wars… I had the personality type that kept us out of wars
because people knew that they weren’t going to mess around here. That’s why I
rebuilt our military. We were strong. We were safe.”

**Going to War Against Planet Earth**

Of course, as has been true from the Korean War on, you just never quite know
what country or countries the United States will be at war with next. And
while such decisions were all too often surprises in the post-Korean War
years, with Donald Trump they should be considered more than surprising. After
all, he’s the president who [swore](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2026/jun/08/what-trump-actually-said-no-war-promise) that he would never
go to war while in the White House. That, of course, was before he started
clobbering one place after another.

In Iran, however, he may have truly met his match. That country’s leadership
now seems eerily intent on enduring what’s happening to them, while
[ensuring](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/07/iran-war-trump-
midterm-ballot) that the American president’s latest war of choice doesn’t
truly end until he and the Republican Party have been clobbered in the
November elections. And hey, with oil prices [still
rising](https://www.npr.org/2026/07/26/nx-s1-5905738/oil-prices-are-climbing-
again-heres-why-this-time-could-be-different) and the cost of crucial goods
generally [going
up](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/08/05/dining/grocery-prices-
shoppers.html) in the United States, while jobs are, for the first time in a
long while,
[shrinking](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/08/07/economy-
shed-23000-jobs-july-labor-market-weakened/), the Iranians clearly know just
what they’re doing -- enduring a hell on earth themselves in order to take
down the world of Donald J. Trump in a potentially big-time fashion.

As Iran’s Mehr News [put it
recently](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/07/iran-war-trump-
midterm-ballot) about You Know Who: “Continuing the war could increase
political and economic pressure on the [U.S.] government and exacerbate the
decline in his popularity. On the other hand, backing down, or moving towards
reducing tensions, could also be interpreted by some of Trump’s supporters as
a retreat from his campaign slogans.”

And honestly, what a world we now find ourselves in! Forget that I’m sweating
in soaring summer temperatures and
[humidity](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/climate-change-is-
turning-up-the-humidity-in-connecticut/3762933/) right here on the East Coast
of the United States, since the temperatures have been [far more
severe](https://abcnews.com/US/extreme-heat-spreads-midwest-east-coast-
remains-hot/story?id=135496657) recently in the Midwest and West. Of course,
parts of our planet are distinctly starting to heat to the boiling point --
and if you don’t believe me, just talk to any of the
[French](https://www.thenation.com/article/environment/this-summers-heat-is-
only-the-beginning/) or [Spanish](https://www.newsweek.com/map-shows-every-
temperature-record-broken-europe-historic-heat-wave-12181952) people who, this
summer, endured fierce wildfires and temperatures that hit 110-112 degrees or
to Canadians in whose country, as I was writing this, [hundreds of
wildfires](https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/en/summary) were still burning, which
“our” president [blames on](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/climate-change-
created-conditions-for-canada-fires-scientists-say-as-trump-blames-
mismanagement) mismanagement. (”If they managed their forests, they wouldn’t
have the fires.”)

And keep in mind that all of this, grim as it might seem, is no more than the
beginning of what could indeed prove to be an all too literal hell on Earth,
given that (among so many other things) “our” president for the next nearly
two and a half years remains intent on pouring fossil fuels into the
atmosphere in a distinctly historic fashion. This planet has, in short, become
the president’s target-practice range.

If this were a fairy tale (even if the fairy tale from hell), you could at
least close the book, put it back on your bookshelf, and go about your
business. Unfortunately, heat and everything that goes with it is now our
business and, barring genuine surprises, will be so in an ever fiercer fashion
for us, our children, and our grandchildren, since our president isn’t just at
war with Iran but distinctly at war with planet Earth and, as in any war,
sooner or later we will all indeed have to pay the price in some fashion or
other.

[Substack](https://tomengelhardt.substack.com/p/the-vietnam-war-redux)._
